title: GSAcc: Accelerate 3D Gaussian Splatting via Depth Speculation and Gaussian-centric Rasterization
problem: GPU-based 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering suffers from insufficient parallelism in sequential pipeline stages and large memory overhead for intermediate results.
motivation: Real-time photorealistic rendering on edge devices requires specialized hardware; dataflow optimization can eliminate serialization bottlenecks.
method: GSAcc introduces Gaussian depth speculation to parallelize preprocessing and sorting. A Gaussian-centric dataflow interleaves preprocessing and rasterization, executing all steps concurrently without storing intermediates. Dedicated hardware accelerates sorting and rasterization.
key_novelty: Gaussian-centric dataflow interleaving preprocessing and rasterization to eliminate intermediate storage and enable full parallelism.
contributions: Gaussian depth speculation enabling parallel preprocessing and sorting
Gaussian-centric dataflow interleaving all rendering stages without intermediate storage
Dedicated hardware acceleration for sorting and rasterization bottlenecks
16,600x PPA improvement vs desktop GPUs, 48.7x energy savings, 2.3x PPA improvement over GSCore
limitations: Evaluation on specific 3DGS scenes; scalability to extremely complex models not discussed.
primary_theme: Hardware accelerator for efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering
